title: Analytic correspondence between multipartite entanglement and quantum phase transitions
authors: Huynh Le Dan Linh, Vu Tuan Hai, Le Bin Ho
abstract: We derive an analytic correspondence between multipartite concentratable entanglement (CE) and quantum phase transitions in one-dimensional quantum spin systems. We prove that CE shares the same analyticity structure as generalized order parameters, identifies the same quantum phases, and, for Gaussian ground states, is completely determined by the same single-particle correlation matrix. Numerical validation on the transverse-field Ising and generalized cluster-Ising models confirms these analytical predictions for both symmetry-breaking and symmetry-protected topological quantum phase transitions. Since CE can be measured directly using a constant-depth parallelized SWAP-test circuit, our results establish CE as an experimentally accessible, model-independent probe of quantum phase transitions without requiring model-specific order parameters.
summary: The paper establishes a deep theoretical link showing that multipartite entanglement (Concentratable Entanglement) behaves identically to traditional order parameters when characterizing Quantum Phase Transitions in 1D spin systems. By proving this correspondence and demonstrating its measurement feasibility via SWAP tests, it offers a universal, model-independent diagnostic tool for studying quantum criticality.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a rigorous, analytic correspondence between multipartite entanglement measures and quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in 1D quantum spin systems.
main_result: It proves that Concentratable Entanglement (CE) shares the same analyticity structure as generalized order parameters (GOPs), identifies the same quantum phases, and serves as an experimentally accessible, model-independent probe for QPTs.
method: The analysis involves deriving theoretical theorems showing shared analytic dependence on single-particle correlation matrices ($\Gamma$) for Gaussian ground states, complemented by numerical validation on specific spin models.
model_or_system: The study focuses on one-dimensional quantum spin systems, specifically the Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM) and generalized cluster-Ising models. The Hamiltonians are local spin-1/2 interactions parameterized by coupling constants ($\lambda$).
key_observables: Concentratable Entanglement ($C(S)$), Generalized Order Parameters (GOPs, $O(\lambda)$), and the single-particle correlation matrix ($\Gamma_{ij}$).
important_parameters: Control parameters $\lambda$ governing the Hamiltonian; critical points where phase transitions occur.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a unique gapped ground state within each quantum phase, and for free-fermion systems, it relies on the analyticity of the Bogoliubov transformation with respect to Hamiltonian parameters.

paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical theorems establishing shared analyticity (Theorem 1), demonstrates phase discrimination capabilities using CE (Theorem 2), and proves an exact correspondence for Gaussian ground states based on $\Gamma$ (Theorem 3). This is validated numerically on TFIM and cluster-Ising models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, entanglement-based diagnostic tool that bypasses the need to calculate model-specific order parameters, making QPT detection more accessible for experimental quantum simulation platforms.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Comparison between the normalized GOP e O (left), normalized CE eC (center), and their absolute difference | e O −eC| (right) for two representative one-dimensional spin models with N = 5: (a) the transverse-field Ising model, and (b) the generalized cluster-Ising model. In all cases, CE accurately reproduces the phase boundaries identified by the corresponding GOP. The normalized root-mean-square deviations are approximately 7% and 8%, respectively. The remaining discrepancies are localized predominantly near the critical manifold, while the agreement within each gapped phase is excellent, consistent with Theorem 1.
